case_name: Padam Singh v State of Uttar Pradesh
respondent:
State of Uttar Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

30 November 1999
Appeal (Crl.) 679 of 1997
The Judgment was delivered by : G. B. Pattanaik, J.
1.  The appellant Padam Singh and his co-accused Desh Raj were convicted by the Sessions Judge, Bulandshahar in Sessions Trial No. 260 of 1980 for the offence under Sections 302, 307, 452, 148, 324 read with Sec, 149 IPC and were sentenced to imprisonment for life for their conviction under Section 302 and other sentences for other offences with the direction that the sentences would run concurrently. Both of them preferred appeals to the High Court but co-accused Desh Raj, died during the pendency of his appeal and, therefore his appeal stood abated. The appeal filed by appellant-Padam Singh was heard by a Bench of Hon'ble Justice G.P. Mathur and Hon'ble Justice Kundan Singh. Hon'ble Justice Mathur, came to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt against the accused appellant and
facts: The appellant Padam Singh and his co-accused Desh Raj were convicted by the Sessions Judge, Bulandshahar in Sessions Trial No. 260 of 1980 for the offence under Sections 302, 307, 452, 148, 324 read with Sec, 149 IPC and were sentenced to imprisonment for life for their conviction under Section 302 and other sentences for other offences with the direction that the sentences would run concurrently.
Both of them preferred appeals to the High Court but co-accused Desh Raj, died during the pendency of his appeal and, therefore his appeal stood abated.
The appeal filed by appellant-Padam Singh was heard by a Bench of Hon'ble Justice G.P. Mathur and Hon'ble Justice Kundan Singh.

Ved Ram lodged the First Information Report, alleging that on 28.9.79 at 6 A.M., while he was lying on a cot in the verandah of his Baithak and deceased Hari Singh was lying on another cot, both were talking to each other, accused Padam Singh, Desh Raj, Lekh Raj and five to six others, entered into the house from the main gate and Desh Raj fired from his gun which hit Hari Singh.
Ved Ram rushed inside his Baithak and closed the door and he also fired from the said Baithak. Firing from both sides continued for a long period.
The accused-assailants then searched for Ved Ram's father and when his wife Vimlesh tried to stop them, she was assaulted by Padam Singh with Farsa.
Raghuraj Singh had taken position on the roof of the house of Sher Singh and he started firing from there.
The accused-assailants, then broke open the wall of the room and went over the roof and escaped through the side lane.
Ved Ram PW1 came out of his Baithak and saw that Hari Singh was lying dead. He also saw one of the assailants Munshi was lying dead.
Even the body of Lekh Raj was also found there; PW1 and others tried to chase the accused persons but could not catch hold of them.
They further found the dead body of another unknown person at a distance of four furlongs.
The prosecution party then came back and lodged the report at 8.30 A.M. in the Police Station, which was at a distance of eight kilometers.
On the basis of the aforesaid F.I R., PW5, Sub-Inspector of Police of Police Station Kakore, commenced investigation.
He held inquest over the dead body of Hari Singh as well on the dead bodies of Lekh Raj and Munshi.
Certain arms and ammunitions were also found near the dead bodies of Munshi and Lekh Raj, which were seized.
He went a distance of four furlongs, where the dead body of the unknown person was lying and held inquest over the same.

The investigation was then taken over by Uma Shanker Singh, who ultimately completed the investigation and submitted the charge-sheet against the two accused persons namely Desh Raj and Padam Singh and on being committed, the accused persons stood their trial in respect of the charges as already started.
The prosecution examined eleven witnesses, including four eye witnesses PWs 1, 2, 3, and 4.
issues: What is the veracity of the prosecution's case?
Can the prosecution establish its case beyond reasonable doubt against the accused?
Is the evidence of the four eye witnesses reliable and trustworthy?
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt against the accused.
The origin and genesis of the prosecution case is doubtful.
The investigation never proceeded against the death of three persons from the accused side, which creates doubt in the prosecution's case.
The four eye witnesses are inimical and their evidence cannot be relied upon.
The Court must examine the veracity of the evidence on record to come to its own conclusion.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution has been able to prove its case successfully with reliable and convincing evidence beyond reasonable shadow of doubt.
The evidence of PWs 1 to 4 is sufficient to bring home the charge.
The Court must bear in mind the innocence and rustic persons hailing from rural areas, when deposed about certain state of affairs.
When the occurrence has taken place in broad day light and there has been no lack of opportunity in identifying the accused persons, the evidence of PWs 1 to 4 is sufficient to bring home the charge.
court_reasoning: The Court must examine the veracity of the evidence on record to come to its own conclusion.
The Court must also bear in mind the innocence and rustic persons hailing from rural areas, when deposed about certain state of affairs.
When the occurrence has taken place in broad day light and there has been no lack of opportunity in identifying the accused persons, the evidence of PWs 1 to 4 is sufficient to bring home the charge.
The Court must be cautious, circumspect and careful while dealing with a case where an accused is charged of murder under Section 302.
holding: The appeal was dismissed by the High Court by majority of two as to one.
The prosecution's case was held to have been established beyond reasonable doubt against the accused.
